slots.label: Plants make their own food
entries: Plants make their own food - light energy from the Sun streams into the leaf, and the green plant builds glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: In: carbon dioxide and water
entries: In: carbon dioxide and water - carbon dioxide enters through tiny pores under the leaf, while water is absorbed by the roots and travels up to the leaf.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Out: glucose and oxygen
entries: Out: glucose and oxygen - with chlorophyll trapping the light, the plant builds glucose as its food and releases oxygen into the air as a by-product.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Energy in, food out
entries: Energy in, food out - light energy powers the change, which is why plants are called producers: they make food for almost all life.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Misconception: oxygen does NOT come from CO2
entries: Misconception: oxygen does NOT come from CO2 - the released oxygen comes from splitting water, while carbon dioxide supplies the carbon for glucose.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Photosynthesis
entries: The process by which green plants make glucose using light energy, taking in carbon dioxide and water and releasing oxygen.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Chlorophyll
entries: The green pigment in leaves that traps the light energy which powers photosynthesis.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Glucose
entries: The sugar the plant builds as food during photosynthesis; it can be used for energy, growth and building new tissue.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Producer
entries: An organism that makes its own food; plants are producers because photosynthesis builds food for almost all life.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
